title: rhus toxicodendron subsp. diversiloba
intro: Rhus toxicodendron subsp. diversiloba, commonly known as Poison Sumac, is a toxic plant native to the southeastern United States, belonging to the Anacardiaceae family. It has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, including its potential health benefits such as treating skin conditions like eczema and dermatitis, as well as reducing fever and inflammation. The therapeutic actions of Poison Sumac are attributed to its ability to stimulate the immune system, reduce pain and swelling, and exhibit antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties. The bioactive constituents of Poison Sumac include saponins, alkaloids, and terpenoids, which contribute to its medicinal properties and have been studied for their potential therapeutic effects.
